svg.aria-label: Tile microarchitecture — who talks on which virtual network
svg.text: Tile microarchitecture — who talks on which virtual network
Two independent protocol agents share one router port. The deadlock argument is visible here: three structurally separate networks, and nothing on VN2 ever waits.
pure function (state, event) -> next state + actions, 13 states
issues on VN0 · accepts VN1 and VN2 · answers on VN2
coherence traffic outranks the core request, always
three writers of a line's state: S1, the VN1 handler, the VN2 handler
Directory agent — home bank for addr[6:5]
pure function (dir state, event) -> next state + actions, 5 states
accepts VN0 and VN2 · forwards on VN1 · answers on VN2
strictly inclusive: an L2 eviction recalls the L1 copies
VN2 in is a true sink — buffered, never back-pressured
three separate packetisers, three separate reassembly paths, three separate credit pools
only the physical flit port is shared, and it is arbitrated per FLIT, not per packet
a blocked VN0 can never hold the injection path a VN2 response needs
5 ports x 6 VCs (2 per vnet), XY routing, credit flow control
N / S / E / W links — flit out, credit back
Virtual networks, numbered by dependency depth
VN0 requests GetS, GetM, PutS, PutM, PutE
VN1 forwards Fwd-GetS, Fwd-GetM, Inv, Recall, Put-Ack
VN2 responses Data, Inv-Ack, WB-Data, Recall-Ack
Solid = sent by this tile. Dashed = received.
hold_vn* is an ordinary pipeline register at hold=0;
above 0 a directed test forces an exact interleaving
without changing the hardware under test (D16).
The directory's responses hold separately from the L1's,
because race R1 needs Data to land after the Inv-Acks.
